title: Why Do Dogs Howl?
description:
That eerie howl isn't random — it's ancient wolf DNA talking.

script: Ever wonder why your dog suddenly throws their head back and howls at absolutely nothing? It's leftover wolf instinct. Wolves howl to communicate across long distances, calling the pack together or marking territory. Your dog inherited that same wiring. A siren, another dog barking far away, even a high-pitched sound can trigger it because their brain interprets it as a howl worth answering. Some dogs also howl when they're anxious or bored, using it the same way wolves use it, to say I'm here, where is everyone else. So next time your dog howls back at an ambulance, know that somewhere deep down, that's a five-thousand-year-old wolf instinct still running the show.
